headline: High-risk shared-write and downstream-action pair: nullclaw can alter files/network while rasa can ingest and act on conversational inputs, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; rasa ingests text/voice via chat channels. A shared workspace or bridged channel could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, MCP server, or message bridge
IF rasa parses nullclaw-generated content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared workspace or bridge between the agents
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent messages
Strip instructions from file and chat payloads before handoff
Use separate MCP servers per agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while rasa handles text/voice and has allowlisted egress. If they share storage or conversation handoff, sensitive data can flow from nullclaw into rasa outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF nullclaw workspace files or secrets are exposed to rasa inputs
IF rasa logs or forwards received text/voice containing secrets
mitigations: Separate storage paths and credentials per agent
Redact secrets before any handoff
Turn off verbose logging on both agents
Restrict rasa channels to non-sensitive conversations
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, shell, and broad egress; rasa is a multi-instance chatbot framework with allowlisted egress. If both touch the same repo, workspace, or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible and can corrupt artifacts. The overlap is enough to treat default coordination as dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, git branch, or database
IF no external locking or lease mechanism serializes their updates
mitigations: Assign disjoint workspaces per agent
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use file locks or a lease file
Commit through a single integration bot
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate web, file, and webhook content, and rasa is a dialogue system that can consume text/voice and route responses through messaging channels. If rasa treats nullclaw output as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into user-facing actions or messages. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF rasa uses nullclaw output as a source of truth
IF downstream handlers send messages or trigger workflows based on that output
mitigations: Require human review before outward-facing actions
Add a verification step between agents
Limit nullclaw output to structured, schema-validated fields
Log source attribution on every derived claim
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs, while rasa handles text and voice with allowlisted egress. If regulated or sensitive conversations are routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show certifications or residency controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets, customer support records, or voice transcripts flows through both agents
IF their logging or retention policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through both agents
Minimize retention on both sides
Mask secrets before storage or replay
Document data-class handling per agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
